rounds.text: Supreme Power Equipment Ltd is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, underscored by a rules-based screen scoring 97 out of 100 with a high-confidence buy rating [E54]. Financial returns significantly outperform sector benchmarks, with a return on equity of 18.72% against a sector median of 11.03% and a return on capital employed of 20.73% compared to 13.04% [E9, E10]. Growth metrics are equally compelling, propelled by compounded sales growth of 46% over the trailing twelve months and net profit growth surging by 53% year-over-year [E15, E57]. Furthermore, working capital efficiency has improved dramatically, with working capital requirements dropping from 94.0 days to 39.1 days and debtor days contracting from 139 to 94.1 days [E50, E51]. Order book visibility is exceptionally robust, backed by an order book exceeding INR 565.80 crores and management guidance targeting full-year revenue between INR 300 crores and INR 350 crores for FY27 [E64, E76]. Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% and borrowings have increased to INR 57 crores in Sep 2026 from INR 50 crores a year prior [E4, E30].

Despite high expectations, the stock’s valuation is heavily extended across multiple metrics, trading at a P/E of 27.29x and an EV/EBITDA of 17.57x, both of which sit at a clear premium to their respective sector benchmarks of 21.11x and 12.02x [E6, E11]. This expensive pricing is compounded by an aggressive price-to-book ratio of 5.16x against a sector benchmark of 2.38x, alongside a total absence of shareholder returns through a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E7]. Beneath the surface of reported profits, the company burned ₹ -32 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026, while borrowings increased to ₹ 57 Cr by September 2026 from ₹ 50 Cr a year prior [E27, E30]. Furthermore, institutional backing has largely evacuated the counter, with foreign institutional holdings plunging from 9.21% to 0.75% and domestic institutional holdings collapsing from 11.31% to 0.23% since December 2023 [E33, E34]. Operating performance also shows underlying vulnerabilities, flagged by potential interest cost capitalization and a historical record of severe volatility marked by a -74.2% peak-to-trough drawdown [E44, E53]. Conceded: the company displays strong top-line sales growth, improved debtor days down to 94.1 days, and a robust return on capital employed of 20.73% beating the sector benchmark [E8, E14, E50].

Conceded: [E4, E6, E7, E11, E27, E30, E33, E34, E44, E53]. While the bear highlights premium valuation multiples and an absence of dividends, those metrics fail to price in superior operational efficiency, demonstrated by an ROA of 9.54%, ROE of 18.72%, and ROCE of 20.73% that comfortably outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. The negative free cash flow of ₹ -32 Cr is eclipsed by robust operating cash flow of ₹ 26 Cr and a strong cash conversion of 1.24x, ensuring that reported profits are entirely backed by actual cash [E25, E26, E27]. The flight of institutional holdings is directly counterbalanced by positive money flow and a promoter stake that has increased to 57.16%, alongside a high relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E32, E35, E42]. Furthermore, the premium valuation is justified by exceptional fundamentals, including 3-year compounded sales growth of 22% and TTM sales growth of 46% [E14, E15].

Conceded: [E8, E9, E10]. While higher returns on capital look attractive on paper, they are undermined by a negative free cash flow of ₹ -32 Cr and a dangerous reliance on debt that has climbed to ₹ 57 Cr, up from ₹ 50 Cr [E27, E30]. The bull points to cash conversion of 1.24x, but this metric ignores the capital intensity of the business, where potential capitalization of interest costs hints at aggressive accounting practices [E25, E53]. Institutional confidence is not counterbalanced by insiders when foreign and domestic institutions have drastically abandoned their stakes from 9.21% down to 0.75% and 11.31% down to 0.23% respectively [E33, E34]. Finally, the premium valuation multiples—including a P/E of 27.29x, P/B of 5.16x, and EV/EBITDA of 17.57x—sit well above sector benchmarks and leave no room for error if growth expectations falter [E6, E7, E11].

Conceded: [E27]. The bear attacks negative free cash flow of ₹ -32 Cr, but this is a natural consequence of aggressive growth and capacity expansion, including the operational ramp-up of the new Kannur facility that pushes total capacity to approximately 9,000 MVA [E70, E72]. The concern over rising borrowings to ₹ 57 Cr is overstated given that debt-to-equity remains at a moderate 0.43x [E28, E30], while profits are fully backed by strong operating cash flow of ₹ 26 Cr and a robust 1.24x cash conversion [E25, E26]. The speculation regarding aggressive accounting via capitalized interest is counterbalanced by an exceptional rules-based screen score of 97 out of 100 [E53, E54]. The institutional exit ignores the powerful validation of positive money flow and insider commitment, with promoters actually increasing their stake to 57.16% [E32, E33, E34, E35].

Conceded: [E32]. The bull dismisses negative free cash flow of ₹ -32 Cr as mere growth pains, yet ignores that borrowings climbed to ₹ 57 Cr while the current ratio sits at a thin buffer of 1.28x [E27, E28, E30, E29]. The defense of interest capitalization as a minor worry glosses over a direct flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost [E53]. Furthermore, the bull leans heavily on the promoter stake increase while glossing over the massive institutional exodus, where foreign and domestic institutional holdings plummeted from 9.21% and 11.31% down to a negligible 0.75% and 0.23% respectively [E33, E34]. Finally, the claim that price-led expectations are fully supported is contradicted by the record showing that price growth recently outpaces profit growth by 4%, meaning expectations are running ahead of delivery [E48].
